solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mormon treats Lady Gaga with first-rate bible

indicators.note: gaga means crazy or senile, so the letters of the two words before it go wild into a new order

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in letters
NT, the New Testament, is a familiar part of the bible

explanation.surface: A churchgoer enjoys buying the pop star Lady Gaga a superb Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Gaga' reads as the singer, but 'Gaga' is the anagram signal working on TREATS LADY to make LATTERDAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints are popularly called Mormons.

clue.text: Information uncovered by The Listener?

definitions.note: an adjective, 'of the ear', the organ by which a listener hears

indicators.note: with its covering stripped off, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a notice is a piece of information posted for people to read

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a piece of news was dug up by the Listener, a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC magazine (and is a crossword series), but here it is simply anyone who listens, i.e. the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the anatomical adjective for things relating to the ear, the organ a listener hears with.

clue.text: Old king not wanting answer

parts.note: off as in 'off one's food' or 'off alcohol', no longer wanting it

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch loses interest in hearing any reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia in England, famous for Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was an ancient Anglo-Saxon ruler, so a monarch from long ago.

clue.text: Indeed, even saving energy gains nothing

indicators.note: gains means takes on something extra, so the next piece is added at the end
saving means keeping something within, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: to be quits is to be even, owing nothing
E is the physics symbol for energy
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Even with economies on power, the result is no profit at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite so is an emphatic phrase of agreement, as is indeed when used as a reply.

clue.text: Shows conjecture on a divided Newcastle?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another is placed above it

parts.note: spec, short for speculation, is a conjecture or a punt
split the city's name into NEW and CASTLE: new then signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of castle

explanation.surface: Someone guesses about a split Newcastle, as if the city were staging events.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks the solver to divide the name Newcastle: its first part, New, works as the anagram signal on its second part, castle, giving TACLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles are grand public displays or performances, which are shows.

clue.text: Quiet Jack left banged-up by judge briefly having priority

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: banged-up is slang for locked away in jail, so these pieces are shut inside the next one
a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: a referee judges a game or a dispute
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: A silent sailor who walked out is jailed by a judge, and his case jumps the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something preferable is to be chosen first, so it takes precedence over the alternatives.

clue.text: Grit breaking up Spitfire flap

indicators.note: breaking means smashing apart, so the letters of the following words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Courage holds as a Spitfire's wing flap breaks up in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' looks like one phrase, but only 'breaking' is the signal; UP is part of the fodder. A Spitfire is the famous British wartime fighter plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a stiff upper lip means showing stoic resolve in adversity, which is grit.

clue.text: What a coincidence Pluto could be described thus

definitions.meaning: the stock remark on meeting someone unexpectedly or finding a surprising connection
Pluto is a dwarf planet, so literally a small world

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said at chance meetings, and Pluto is a tiny planetary body, a little globe.

clue.text: Random act cost his supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, nimbly or flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: An arbitrary act cost him his provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the noun or verb, but is the adverb 'in a supple way', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stochastic is the technical term for processes governed by chance, so random.

clue.text: Some choirboys look this way

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following word are used, a run concealed inside it

explanation.surface: A few of the choristers glance in this direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi is a call used to attract someone's attention, telling them to look over here.

clue.text: Express firm seeking excitement

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective, quick, as an express train is
... meaning fixed and secure, as in stuck ...
a ... set lives a racy, pleasure-seeking life

explanation.surface: A courier company is looking for thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has three senses: speedy, firmly fixed, and dissolute in pursuit of pleasure.

clue.text: Secondly, stipple with pencil and draw

indicators.note: the second letter of each of the next words is taken

explanation.surface: An artist's instructions: next, dot the paper with a pencil and sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' reads as sketching, but it is the noun: a match ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a game finishing with equal scores, which is a draw.

clue.text: Part of the ocean seen from piece of ground around a sunken basin

indicators.note: the first piece goes round what follows, enclosing it

parts.note: an area is a piece of land or ground

indicators.note: sunk can mean ruined, so these letters are wrecked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: From a plot of land you can see a depression in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian Sea is a region of the Indian Ocean between Arabia and India.

clue.text: Strange stuff, business — 24's stern, getting one demoted

parts.note: biz is a slang shortening of business, as in show biz

indicators.note: in a down answer, a letter demoted is moved lower down the word

parts.note: 24 across is NICE, the French city, where the stern or rear is called arrière
I, the Roman numeral, stands for one

explanation.surface: Odd goings-on at a firm: the stern of the vessel at 24, with someone losing rank.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points at the answer to 24 across, the city of Nice, so 'stern' needs French: ARRIERE, and moving its I lower gives ARRERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarrerie is a collective noun for oddity, bizarre things or behaviour.

clue.text: Forbidden fruit pips oddly put in water

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Adam's ale is a jocular old name for water

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the following word, first and third, are kept

explanation.surface: Seeds from the banned fruit are dropped into water.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is an old humorous term for plain water.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx's bulge is named for the forbidden fruit said to have lodged in Adam's throat in Eden.

clue.text: Search force missing danger

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to frisk is to search someone by running hands over them
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A police search party is short-staffed and in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk is a hazard, the chance of harm, which is a danger.

clue.text: Monk, for instance, to enliven bishop, say

parts.note: to jazz something up is to make it livelier
a bishop is a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: A monk, perhaps, livening up a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monk' suggests a religious brother, but it is Thelonious Monk, the jazz pianist.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelonious Monk was a celebrated jazz pianist, an example of a jazz musician.

clue.text: Quibble regularly, stopping to seize rule by violence?

indicators.note: stopping up something means filling a gap within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: to claw is to grab or seize

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: Constantly nitpicking, someone halts the attempt at a violent seizure of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Club law is government by force, literally rule by the cudgel.

clue.text: Weak and mischievous after whiskey

indicators.note: the first piece comes after the second

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
impish means mischievous, like an imp

explanation.surface: Feeble and playful after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimpish describes someone feeble and lacking courage, a wimp.

clue.text: Religious follower mostly backing despot

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters are read backwards
most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a Rasta is a follower of the Rastafarian religion

explanation.surface: A devout believer largely supports a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the autocratic ruler of Russia, a byword for despotism.

clue.text: Entry slips spoiled as per lifelong non-union member

definitions.note: an adjective: in the manner of a woman who never marries

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the letters of these words are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Ballot slips are spoiled in the way a lifelong non-member of a trade union might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-union member' suggests trade unions; it means someone never united in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinsterly means in the manner of a spinster, an unmarried woman, one never joined in wedlock.

clue.text: Festival finishing, just like that

indicators.note: the finishing letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: The fair ends, just like that.
explanation.definitionFit: Tet is the Vietnamese lunar New Year celebration, a festival.

clue.text: Valley formed in beginnings of recent ice age

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the next words is taken

explanation.surface: A valley carved out at the start of the latest glacial period.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long, narrow inlet formed when a river valley is drowned by the sea.

clue.text: Delicate new diamonds — in round hollow case

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Fragile new gems sit inside a round case with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: There is a second wordplay: 'in round' is IN reversed, NI, and 'hollow case' is CASE emptied, CE, giving NICE again.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean subtle or fine, as in a nice distinction, which is delicate.

clue.text: In which players may be highly strung?

definitions.text: In which players may be highly strung?

parts.words: In which players may be highly strung?
parts.note: highly strung suggests nervous actors, but marionettes are literally hung from strings

explanation.definitionFit: In a marionette performance the performers are dangling on strings from above.

clue.text: Article found in half of gooey piece of cake

indicators.note: the article is found within the next piece
only the second half of the word is kept

parts.note: cheesy can mean gooey, sentimentally soppy
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A single item turns up in part of a sticky slice of gateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for something simple to do.

clue.text: Stitch trapping male diver

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the next piece goes within

parts.note: to stitch is to sew

explanation.surface: A seam catches a man who dives.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small duck that feeds by diving, one of the sawbills.

clue.text: Spot nerve cut by inferior alloy

indicators.note: the pair is cut into by the next piece, which goes between them

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark
steel is nerve, courage, as in steel oneself
less can mean lower in rank, inferior

explanation.surface: A blemish of courage weakened by poor metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainless steel is a corrosion-resisting iron alloy containing chromium.
